pr_body:
This allows private constructors on the Types to be trimmed.

Fix #50353

issue_context.title: Lack of DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes for any default constructor forces keeping unused types
issue_context.body:
One example is https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/72f57669b2ca032c4eb86251e2cadec611426ded/src/mono/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/RuntimeType.Mono.cs#L1838 which has an annotation for any constructor even if only the default constructor is considered. This keeps unnecessary dependencies like `System.Runtime.Serialization.StreamingContext` via `EnumComparer<T>` private ctors. I far as I know there is no workaround for this.

/cc @eerhardt @vitek-karas

I couldn't figure out the best area label to add to this issue. If you have write-permissions please help me learn by adding exactly one [area label](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/master/docs/area-owners.md).

Looking through all the callsites of `CreateInstanceForAnotherGenericParameter`, it looks like either all the types passed into it already have a public parameterless constructor, or they are internal classes, so we can make the constructor public on them.

The only one that doesn't look this way is 

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/82ca681cbac89d813a3ce397e0c665e6c051ed67/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Collections/Generic/EqualityComparer.cs#L180-L183

But that class isn't public in a contract - just in the implementation, and the comment indicates it needs to be public due to binary serialization. Since this isn't in a public contract, we could make its parameterless constructor public.

Then we can change `CreateInstanceForAnotherGenericParameter` implementation to only look for public parameterless constructors.

> Then we can change CreateInstanceForAnotherGenericParameter implementation to only look for public parameterless constructors.

I guess that could work.
I can put up a PR after https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/50232 is merged.

review_comments:
This is a public API change, right?
I think it's not a problem - but it will probably come with "process"...

> This is a public API change, right?

No. This type isn't really "public". It isn't exposed by a ref/contract assembly. https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/search/?scope=.NET&terms=EnumEqualityComparer

It is just public in the implementation assembly because of this comment

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/82ca681cbac89d813a3ce397e0c665e6c051ed67/src/libraries/System.Private.CoreLib/src/System/Collections/Generic/EqualityComparer.cs#L180-L181
The other "Needs to be public to support binary serialization compatibility" types in this file just depend on the compiler to generate the default public ctor. It would be nice to be consistent.
Oh, ok - this one is special since it implements ISerializable.
